docs.title: Quota Dashboard Runbook
docs.text:
How to look after the Quota Dashboard (the quoting tool for Jordan Select Tours and Jordan Direct Tours), and what to do when something goes wrong. Written so that anyone on duty can follow it, step by step, even if they have never done it before.

Something is broken right now?

Go straight to The site is down: first five minutes.

docs.title: Pick what you need
docs.text: I want to... Go to Check that Quota is healthy Daily health check Fix Quota when staff cannot open it The site is down Fix one thing that fails (a PDF, an e-mail, a picture) Common errors Put a new version live Release a new version Undo a bad version Go back to an earlier version Check the backups Backups Know how staff and clients get in How staff and clients reach it Look after the office Mac itself The office Mac Type commands on the Mac from my own computer Connect to the server Change a password or key Passwords and keys Bring the data back from a backup Restore the database

docs.title: How to use these pages
docs.text:
• Do the steps in order, one at a time. Do not skip a step because it looks done.
  • Grey boxes are commands. Click the copy button at the box's top right, paste it into the Terminal with ⌘ V, and press Return.
  • After most steps there is a picture of a Terminal window. It shows what you type (marked you type this) and what comes back. Green is what you want to see. Red means something is wrong: look at the table If you see something else at the bottom of the page.
  • The pictures are examples. Dates, times and numbers on your screen will be different. That is normal.

docs.title: Words used on these pages
docs.text: Word What it means The office Mac The Mac mini in the office that runs Quota. Every command on this site is typed on it. Terminal The Mac app where you type commands. Open it with ⌘ Space, type Terminal, press Return. The Quota folder The folder ~/quota on the office Mac. Every command on this site is typed there. Box (container) One part of Quota running on the Mac: frontend (the website), backend (the brain), db (the database), backup (nightly copies), mail (a test mail catcher). Release Putting a new version of Quota live, with a button on GitHub. Tunnel A safe link from the office Mac to Cloudflare, so people can reach Quota from outside without opening the router.

docs.title: Typing the commands
docs.text:
The live copy of Quota is called quota and uses two settings files, so many commands start like this:

docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env

Always copy the whole command from the page. If you leave out a part, the command talks to an empty copy and shows nothing.

docs.title: How a new version arrives
docs.text: Code changes are tested by robots on GitHub, but nothing reaches the office until someone presses Release to production. The office Mac then installs it by itself within minutes: it takes a backup first, updates, checks itself, and goes back to the old version on its own if anything fails. See How a change goes live.

docs.title: How people reach it
docs.text:
Who Address What protects it Staff, office and home https://quota.selectdmc.com A one-time code sent to a work e-mail, then the Quota sign-in Clients trip.jordanselect.com (JST) and trip.jdtours.com (JDT) Only the map, the online offer and pictures; nothing else answers

See How staff and clients reach it.

docs.title: The golden rules
docs.text:
1. Never delete a Docker volume. Never run docker compose down -v or docker volume prune. That erases the database.
  2. Never start or stop other servers on ports 80, 5190 or 8010. They belong to the live Quota.
  3. Read the message before you act. Change one thing at a time.
  4. Write down what you did, with the times.
  5. When unsure, stop and ask. Waiting is safer than guessing.

docs.title: Who to contact
docs.text:
(Name, phone, role. Fill this in.)

Keep this site free of secrets

This site is public. Never write passwords, keys, IP addresses or customer data here. The pictures on it are made-up examples.

docs.title: Connect to the server
docs.text:
When to use this: A page says "on the office Mac", and you are not sitting at it. Time it takes: 5 minutes (the first time: 15) You need: Your own computer, to be in the office (or on the office VPN), and the server address and your username from the person who manages the server.

If you are sitting at the office Mac, skip to Go to the Quota folder.

The address and username are not on this site

This site is public. Ask the developer, or look in the team password manager. Below, replace <username> and <server-address> with what they give you.

docs.title: The first time only: make your key
docs.text:
A key is how the Mac knows it is you. You make it once on your own computer.

  1. Open the Terminal on your own computer. On a Mac: ⌘ Space, type Terminal, press Return. On Windows: open PowerShell from the Start menu.

  2. Copy this, paste it, press Return:

    ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your-name-laptop"

  3. It asks where to save: press Return. It asks for a passphrase: type one you will remember, press Return, then type it again. Nothing shows while you type. That is normal.

  4. Show your key:

    cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

  5. Copy the whole line that starts with ssh-ed25519 and send it to the person who manages the server. Wait until they say it has been added.

Only ever send the line from the file ending in .pub

The other file, without .pub, is your private key. Never send it or paste it anywhere.

docs.title: Every time: connect
docs.text:
1. In the Terminal on your own computer:

    ssh <username>@<server-address>

  2. The first time only, it asks Are you sure you want to continue connecting? Type yes and press Return.

  3. Type your key's passphrase if it asks. You are now typing on the office Mac.

docs.title: Go to the Quota folder
docs.text:
Every command on this site is typed in the Quota folder.

cd ~/quota
ls

You should see

backend, deploy and docs in the list. If you do, you are in the right place.

docs.title: When you are done
docs.text: Type exit and press Return. The connection closes.

docs.title: If you see something else
docs.text: You see Do this Connection timed out You are not in the office or on the VPN, or the Mac is off. Connection refused The address is wrong, or remote login is off on the Mac. Ask the developer. Permission denied (publickey) Your key was not added yet, or the username is wrong. REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED Stop. Do not type yes. Ask the developer. No such file or directory after cd ~/quota You are connected to the wrong machine or user. Ask the developer.

docs.title: Stay safe
docs.text:
• Use only your own key. If your laptop is lost, tell the server manager at once so your key is removed.
  • Do not run commands you do not understand. Never run docker compose down -v or docker volume prune.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: How staff and clients reach it
docs.text:
When to use this: Staff or clients cannot open Quota from outside, or you want to know how the doors work. Time it takes: 5 minutes to read You need: For changes, the Cloudflare account that holds the domains, and SSH access.

Quota runs on the office Mac. Nobody reaches it through an open router port. Two Cloudflare tunnels run on the Mac and carry the traffic out to Cloudflare, which gives the https address and certificate.

docs.title: The two doors
docs.text:
Staff Clients Address https://quota.selectdmc.com https://trip.jordanselect.com (JST), https://trip.jdtours.com (JDT) Tunnel in Cloudflare quota-staff quota-maps Container on the Mac quota-staff-tunnel quota-tunnel Who gets in Only people Cloudflare Access lets through: a one-time code sent to a work e-mail address Anyone with a link What answers All of Quota, after the Quota sign-in Only the route map, the online offer and offer pictures. Every other path answers 404.

Each brand has its own client address so a client never sees the other brand's name. Quota picks the address from the order's company (CLIENT_URL_SELECT and CLIENT_URL_DIRECT in deploy/.env).

The client door serves pictures only

The pictures folder also holds old proposal files with client names and prices. The client door answers only for picture files (jpg, png, webp and the like) and 404 for anything else in it.

docs.title: Check the doors
docs.text:
From a phone on mobile data (not the office Wi-Fi):

  • https://trip.jordanselect.com/health answers {"status":"ok"}.
  • https://trip.jordanselect.com/api/v1/auth/me answers 404. That is right: the client door must not reach sign-in.
  • https://quota.selectdmc.com shows the Cloudflare page asking for an e-mail address, never Quota straight away.

On the office Mac, in the Terminal:

docker ps --format '{{.Names}}  {{.Status}}' | grep tunnel

You should see

quota-staff-tunnel and quota-tunnel, both Up.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this Both addresses fail, but Quota works inside the office A tunnel is down. docker start quota-staff-tunnel quota-tunnel. If it stops again, read docker logs --tail=50 quota-tunnel. Staff see a plain 403 page from Quota's address Something else is answering on port 5190 (a test server someone started). Tell the developer; never stop the live boxes. Staff get no code e-mail Their address is not in the Cloudflare Access policy, or the code went to spam. Check Zero Trust › Access in Cloudflare. A client's map link opens but stays blank An old copy of the map is stuck in their browser. A hard reload (Shift + reload) clears it. A client link shows the office address The link was made before the client addresses were set. Copy it again from the order.

The tunnel tokens

Each tunnel has a token in a file next to its start script on the Mac. A token is a password: never put it in chat, e-mail or git. To replace one, make a new token in Cloudflare (Zero Trust › Networks › Tunnels) and restart the tunnel with it.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Common errors: PDF, e-mail, pictures, search
docs.text:
When to use this: Quota works, but one thing fails. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: The Terminal on the office Mac for some fixes (connect if you are not at it).

Find what you see in the first column. If a fix says "restart the backend", type this in the Quota folder:

cd ~/quota
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env restart backend
You see What it means Do this 503 pdf_unavailable when opening a PDF The PDF maker inside the backend failed Restart the backend. If it comes back, tell the developer: the version needs fixing, then go back. 503 mail_unavailable when sending an offer The e-mail settings are wrong or the mail server is down Tell the developer. Staff can still send offers from their own mailbox in Compose. 503 media_unavailable on a picture upload The pictures folder cannot be reached Restart the backend. If it repeats, tell the developer (the MEDIA_ROOT setting). Offers show no pictures Same as above Same as above. Mailbox search finds words but not meanings The search helper (Ollama) is not running The office Mac, step 4. Staff get no new-mail pop-ups Their browser does not allow notifications In the browser: the padlock left of the address → Notifications → Allow. A password-reset or reminder e-mail from Quota never arrives Quota's own e-mails still go to a test mail catcher on the Mac Known: a real sending mailbox is still to be set up. An administrator resets the password instead (next line). "locked" at sign-in Five wrong passwords in fifteen minutes Wait fifteen minutes, or an administrator sets a new password in Administration → Users.

docs.title: If it is still wrong
docs.text:
Copy the last 50 lines of the backend's messages and send them to the developer:

docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=50 backend

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Restore the database from a backup
docs.text:
When to use this: Data was lost or damaged, and the developer agreed to go back to a backup. Time it takes: 20 minutes You need: The Terminal on the office Mac (connect if you are not at it).

This replaces everything in the live database

Anything entered after the backup was taken is lost. Do this only when the developer agrees. Tell staff to stop using Quota first.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] The developer agreed.
  • [ ] Staff were told to stop using Quota.
  • [ ] You know which day to go back to.

docs.title: 1. Go to the Quota folder and find the backup
docs.text:
cd ~/quota
ls deploy/backups | grep sql.gz | tail -3

Pick the file of the day you want, for example quota_2026-11-11_0200.sql.gz (11 November, 02:00). After a release there is also a pre-update_...sql.gz from just before it.

docs.title: 2. Stop everything that writes to the database
docs.text: docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env stop backend backup

docs.title: 3. Empty the database
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -T db psql -U postgres -c 'DROP DATABASE quota' -c 'CREATE DATABASE quota'

You should see

DROP DATABASE then CREATE DATABASE.

docs.title: 4. Load the backup
docs.text:
Change the file name to the one you picked in step 1, then run it:

gunzip -c deploy/backups/quota_2026-11-11_0200.sql.gz | docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -T db psql -U postgres quota

Many lines scroll past. That is normal. It takes a few minutes.

docs.title: 5. Start everything again
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env start backend backup
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend alembic upgrade head

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps --format "table {{.Service}}\t{{.Status}}"

Then sign in, open a recent order and its offer. Tell staff the date and time the data goes back to, so they can enter again anything newer.

docs.title: If you see something else
docs.text:
You see Do this database "quota" is being accessed by other users Step 2 did not stop everything. Do step 2 again, then step 3. gzip: not in gzip format or No such file The file name is wrong. Copy it again from step 1. service "db" is not running docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d db, wait a minute, then step 3 again. Errors about missing columns after the restore Do the second line of step 5 again.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: The server is gone
docs.text:
When to use this: The machine died, was stolen, or its disk is destroyed. Time it takes: About an hour, plus downloads You need: GitHub access to both repositories, a new Mac with OrbStack (or a Linux machine with Docker), the settings file (deploy/.env) from the team password manager, the newest backup copy stored off the server, and the pictures folder.

This is why copies must be kept off the server

If every backup was on the dead machine, the data may be gone. Check laptops, cloud drives, and colleagues first.

A job for the developer

Rebuilding a lost machine needs the developer. This page is the order of the work, so nothing is forgotten.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Prepare a new machine. On a Mac, set it up as The office Mac describes.
  2. Install it by following First install. Use the saved deploy/.env instead of writing a new one: it holds MAIL_SECRET_KEY, without which every mailbox must be connected again.
  3. Put the pictures folder back and point MEDIA_ROOT at it.
  4. Restore the data with Restore the database, using your newest backup.
  5. Start the two tunnels on the new machine with their tokens (see How staff and clients reach it). Staff and client addresses then work unchanged.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• You can sign in, open a recent quote, and view an offer with pictures.
  • A fresh backup exists and is copied off the machine.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this No backup can be found Check every device and cloud account the team uses. Tell the developer immediately. The newest backup is old Restore it anyway, then have staff re-enter newer work.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: The site is down: first five minutes
docs.text:
When to use this: Staff cannot open Quota, or every page shows errors. Time it takes: 5 minutes to find the cause You need: The Terminal on the office Mac (connect if you are not at it).

Stay calm, change one thing at a time

The data is safe in the database. Most problems are fixed by a restart. Do not delete anything.

docs.title: 1. Is it Quota, or the way in?
docs.text: Ask someone in the office to open Quota on the office network. If it works there but not from home, the problem is the tunnel, not Quota: go to How staff and clients reach it.

docs.title: 2. Go to the Quota folder
docs.text:
cd ~/quota

If this says No such file or directory, you are not on the office Mac. See Connect to the server.

docs.title: 3. Which box is in trouble?
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps --format "table {{.Service}}\t{{.Status}}"

A box in trouble says Restarting, Exited or unhealthy, or is missing from the list:

docs.title: 4. Match what you see
docs.text: You see What it means Do this Cannot connect to the Docker daemon OrbStack, the app that runs the boxes, is closed The office Mac Every box says Up, but the site does not load The boxes are fine; it is the way in How staff and clients reach it db is not running The database stopped Do step 5. Check the disk with df -h /. If it will not start: Restore backend keeps restarting Often the database is down, or a setting is wrong Do step 5, then read its messages (step 6) Pages load, but actions give 502 The website cannot reach the backend Do step 5 Staff see a plain 403 page A test server took Quota's port Tell the developer. Do not stop the live boxes. One feature fails: a PDF, an e-mail, a picture Not the whole site Common errors It broke right after a release The new version Go back to an earlier version The Mac does not answer at all Off, or the network is down The server is gone

docs.title: 5. Restart (keeps all data)
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env restart

Wait one minute, then do step 3 again. If a box is still in trouble, stop it all and start it again:

docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env down
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d

Never add -v to down

down -v erases the database.

docs.title: 6. Still broken? Read the messages
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=100 backend

Copy the last 30 lines and send them to the developer.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
curl http://localhost/health
curl http://localhost/api/v1/health/db

Then sign in and open an order.

docs.title: After it is fixed
docs.text:
• Write down what happened, what you did, and the times.
  • Tell the team it is back.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: How a change reaches the office (the pipeline)
docs.text: When to use this: You want to know what the green ticks and red crosses on GitHub mean, and how a change reaches the office. Time it takes: 5 minutes to read

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
push to main ─► CI: style check + tests ─► builds the new version
                Security: secrets, libraries, known holes
you press "Release to production" ─► the office server installs it within minutes
   (backup first, then update, then checks; if anything is wrong it goes back by itself)

Nothing goes live in the office until someone presses Release to production.

The staging copy is switched off

Since 8 November 2026 a tested version goes straight to Release. See The staging copy to bring it back.

docs.title: The robots on GitHub
docs.text:
Open the repository on GitHub and click the Actions tab at the top. Each run shows a green tick, a red cross or a yellow dot.

Robot When What it does CI Every push and pull request Checks the code style and runs the tests. On main, when they pass, builds the new version. Security Every push, and every Monday Looks for passwords committed by mistake, libraries with known security holes, and holes in the built version. Release to production Only when someone presses it Marks the newest tested version as the one the office server should run. You see Meaning Green tick on CI Tests passed; the new version is built and waiting for Release. Red cross on CI A test or style check failed. Nothing was built; the office stays as it was. Tell the developer. Red cross on Security A library needs updating or something looks like a password. Not urgent for the site, but tell the developer this week. Yellow dot Still running. Wait.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Try a change before it goes live: The staging copy
  • Put it live: Release a new version

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: First install
docs.text:
When to use this: Setting up Quota Dashboard on a new machine, or after the server is gone. Time it takes: 45 minutes You need: A Mac with OrbStack (or Linux with Docker and the compose plugin), about 3 GB of disk, a GitHub token with only read:packages, the saved deploy/.env from the password manager, and the pictures folder (images/) on the machine.

A job for the developer

This page is for setting up a whole new machine. Follow it with the developer on the phone if you can.

The machine does not build anything: it downloads the versions the robots built and tested.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] On a Mac, set it up as The office Mac describes first.
  • [ ] Keep the Quota folder outside Documents, Desktop and Downloads (macOS blocks background jobs there). ~/quota is right.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Get the deploy folder.
git clone git@github.com:AbuEnzo/quota-dashboard-backend.git ~/quota
cd ~/quota/deploy
  1. Let the machine download the versions. Quota keeps its own GitHub sign-in in this folder:
mkdir -p .docker
DOCKER_CONFIG=$PWD/.docker docker login ghcr.io -u <github-user>

Paste the read-only token when it asks for the password. Nothing shows while you paste.

![It answers Login Succeeded](../img/term/login.png)
  1. The settings file. Copy back the saved one. Only for a brand-new install, start from the example instead and fill in every value (nano .env):
cp .env.example .env      # brand-new install only

On the office Mac it must contain QUOTA_COMPOSE_EXTRA=compose.office.yml.

  1. First start. The same script that updates: it downloads, creates the database tables and starts everything.
./update.sh
  1. Brand-new install only: the catalogue and the first administrator. Choose a strong password in place of choose-one.
cd ~/quota
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend python scripts/import_legacy.py
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -e SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD='choose-one' backend python scripts/seed_admin.py admin@example.com "Administrator"

When moving to a new machine, restore the database instead.

  1. Turn on the schedules (updates, backups, the weekly test):
cd ~/quota/deploy && ./install-macos.sh
  1. Start the tunnels so staff and clients can reach it. See How staff and clients reach it.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
curl http://localhost/health
curl http://localhost/api/v1/health/db

Then open https://quota.selectdmc.com and sign in.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this unauthorized while downloading Step 2 again; the token needs read:packages. set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in deploy/.env The settings file is missing a value. Edit deploy/.env. set MEDIA_ROOT in deploy/.env Point it at the pictures folder. network quota-net not found Create it once: docker network create quota-net, then step 4 again. Import cannot reach the legacy database The old database address is wrong or not reachable from the container. Ask the developer. Anything else Site is down

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Go back to an earlier version
docs.text:
When to use this: A new version is live, but something in it is wrong, and you want the one before. Time it takes: 5 minutes You need: A GitHub account with write access. No Terminal needed.

Going back does not undo database changes

Database changes only move forward, and they are written so the earlier version keeps working. If it ever does not, the developer can restore the backup the Mac took just before the update (pre-update_... in the backups folder).

docs.title: 1. Find the name of the version you want
docs.text:
Every release is kept under a name like prod-20261111-1302 (the date, then the time in UTC, which is Amman time minus 3 hours).

  1. Open GitHub, go to the quota-dashboard-backend repository.
  2. On the right side of its main page, under Packages, click quota-backend.
  3. Find the version from before the bad release. Copy its name that starts with prod- and is not just prod.

docs.title: 2. Release that version
docs.text:
1. In the same repository, click Actions → Release to production (left list) → Run workflow (right).
  2. In the box that says main, delete main and paste the name you copied, for example prod-20261110-0915.
  3. Click the green Run workflow button.
  4. If the screens were also changed in the bad release, do the same in quota-dashboard-frontend, with the name from its quota-frontend package.
  5. Wait about 5 minutes.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• The release run on GitHub shows a green tick.
  • Sign in to Quota and check the problem is gone.

Back to normal later

The next time someone releases with main, the office gets the latest version again. Tell the developer what was wrong so it is fixed first.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this The release run is red: "not a tag" or "not found" The name is wrong. Copy it again from Packages. Errors about missing columns The database is ahead of the code. Tell the developer.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: The staging copy
docs.text:
When to use this: You want to try a change on real data before it reaches the office. Time it takes: however long you need to try it

Switched off since 8 November 2026

The staging copy was stopped so only the live Quota runs on the Mac. Its data is kept. Until it is back, changes go from the tests straight to Release a new version, so try them on a developer's test copy first.

To bring it back (the developer does this, on the office Mac):

mv .env.staging.off .env.staging
./install-macos.sh

Then refresh its data (below), because it was copied from the live Quota on 8 November.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A second Quota on the same server, on port 8080 of the server's office address. Every change that passes the tests is installed there automatically within minutes. Its data is a copy of the real Quota.

docs.title: What is switched off on staging
docs.text:
So nothing you do there reaches a client, a hotel or another system:

  • No e-mail leaves. Everything "sent" lands in a mail catcher on the server instead.
  • Mailboxes are not read and cannot be opened from staging.
  • No reminders go to clients, and no daily digest.
  • Nothing is written to the CRM or the old Access system.
  • Pictures are read-only. Uploading a picture fails on staging; that is expected.

docs.title: Refresh its data
docs.text: Its data does not follow the real Quota by itself. The developer refreshes it from the real one when needed (the commands are in deploy/README.md, "The staging copy").

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
When it works: Release a new version.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Release a new version
docs.text:
When to use this: The developer says a change is ready and tested, and asks for it to go live. Time it takes: 5 minutes You need: A GitHub account with write access to the two Quota repositories. No Terminal needed.

Staff may see a pause of under a minute

Quota restarts while the new version starts. Release outside busy hours when you can.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] The developer says the change is ready.
  • [ ] On GitHub, the repository's Actions tab shows a green tick on the latest CI run on main. A red cross means it is not ready: stop and tell the developer.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open GitHub and go to the quota-dashboard-backend repository.
  2. Click the Actions tab (at the top, next to Pull requests).
  3. In the list on the left, click Release to production.
  4. On the right, click the grey Run workflow button. A small box opens.
  5. Leave Branch: main and leave the box under it saying main. Click the green Run workflow button.
  6. If the developer says the screens changed too, do steps 1 to 5 again in the quota-dashboard-frontend repository.
  7. Wait about 5 minutes. The office Mac checks every 2 minutes, takes a backup, updates and starts the new version.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• On GitHub, the new Release to production run shows a green tick.
  • Open Quota, sign in, open an order and its offer.
  • If you are at the office Mac: tail -3 ~/Library/Logs/quota-update.log ends with done: (see the picture on The office Mac).

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
The Mac checks the new version itself. If it does not start properly, it puts the previous version back on its own.

You see Do this The release run has a red cross Nothing changed in the office. Check you left main in the box, and try again once. Then tell the developer. Green tick, but after 10 minutes Quota still has the old version The Mac could not download it. See Quota's GitHub sign-in. The new version runs but something is wrong in it Go back to an earlier version.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
When to use this: To know where the copies are, and to check they are being made. Time it takes: 5 minutes You need: The Terminal on the office Mac (connect if you are not at it).

Not finished: only one copy exists today

As of 11 November 2026 the backup SSD and the online copy (Cloudflare R2) are not set up, and neither are the warning e-mails. So every copy stays on the office Mac, the 03:15 job fails every night with "no destination", and nobody is told if something goes wrong. If the Mac is lost, the data is lost. Until this is done, check by hand every week (below). The steps to set them up are in deploy/README.md in the Quota repository, under "Backup and restore" and "Monitoring".

docs.title: What is automatic
docs.text: When What Where Every night, 02:00 The database (about 130 MB) and Quota's own files (offer PDFs, mail attachments) On the Mac, in ~/quota/deploy/backups (30 days of database copies, 7 of files) Before every release The database Same folder, named pre-update_... Every night, 03:15 Everything above, plus the offer pictures The backup SSD and Cloudflare R2, once set up Every Sunday A test: the newest copy is loaded into a scratch database and checked Nothing kept

docs.title: 1. Last night's copy exists
docs.text:
cd ~/quota
ls deploy/backups | grep sql.gz | tail -3

You should see

The last line has today's date, for example quota_2026-11-11_0200.sql.gz.

docs.title: 2. The copy off the Mac
docs.text:
tail -2 ~/Library/Logs/quota-offsite.log

Today it says PROBLEM: no destination set up. That is the unfinished part above:

Once the SSD or R2 is set up, the lines say SSD: done and R2: done.

docs.title: Take a copy by hand
docs.text:
Before anything risky, in the Quota folder:

docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -T db pg_dump -U postgres quota | gzip > deploy/backups/quota_manual.sql.gz

It takes about a minute and prints nothing when it works.

Keep these two safe, outside the Mac

The settings file deploy/.env and the backup encryption password are not in the backups. Keep both in the password manager. Without them the mailboxes cannot be opened and the online copy cannot be read.

docs.title: If you see something else
docs.text:
You see Do this No file with today's date The nightly backup stopped. Check the backup box: Daily health check, step 2. "SSD is not there (drive unplugged?)" Plug the SSD back in. It is checked again the next night. "only N GB free" on the SSD Tell the developer. "R2: copying ... failed" Internet down that night, or the R2 key expired. Tell the developer if it repeats.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Daily health check
docs.text: When to use this: Every morning, or whenever you want to be sure Quota is OK. Time it takes: 1 minute for the quick check, 5 minutes for the full one You need: A browser. For the full check: the Terminal on the office Mac (connect if you are not at it).

docs.title: Quick check (no Terminal)
docs.text:
1. Open https://quota.selectdmc.com and sign in.
  2. Open a recent order, then its offer.

You should see

The order and the offer open normally. If they do, Quota is fine and you can stop here.

docs.title: 1. Go to the Quota folder
docs.text: cd ~/quota

docs.title: 2. Are all the boxes running?
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps --format "table {{.Service}}\t{{.Status}}"

You should see

Five lines: backend, backup, db, frontend and mail, each saying Up. The hours and days will differ.

docs.title: 3. Does Quota answer?
docs.text:
curl http://localhost/health
curl http://localhost/api/v1/health/db

You should see

{"status":"ok"}, then a line with "database":"ok".

docs.title: 4. Was last night's backup made?
docs.text:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=3 backup

You should see

A line backup: wrote /backups/quota_<today's date>_0200.sql.gz. The date must be today's (it runs at 02:00).

docs.title: 5. Is there enough disk space?
docs.text:
df -h /

You should see

More than 20Gi under Avail. Below that, tell the developer this week. Below 10Gi, tell them today: a full disk stops the database.

docs.title: If you see something else
docs.text:
You see Do this The quick check fails The site is down A box says Restarting, Exited, or is missing The site is down curl says Connection refused The site is down No backup line with today's date, or pg_dump failed Check the disk (step 5), then tell the developer. Less than 20Gi free Tell the developer. Never delete Docker volumes to make room.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: The office Mac
docs.text:
When to use this: The Mac was restarted or updated, someone installed something on it, or a new version did not arrive after a release. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: A seat at the Mac, or the Terminal on it (connect).

Quota runs on the Mac mini in the office, from the folder ~/quota. Never run it from any other folder.

docs.title: What must always be true
docs.text: What Why OrbStack is open, and set to Start at login It runs every Quota box and both tunnels. They come back by themselves when it starts. A user is logged in, and the Mac never sleeps The update and backup jobs run only while someone is logged in. The Mac starts by itself after a power cut So Quota comes back with nobody in the office. Ollama is running The mailbox search by meaning uses it. Docker Desktop is not used If it is opened, it takes over and stops the boxes and the updates (this happened on 9 November 2026).

docs.title: 1. OrbStack is in charge
docs.text:
docker context ls

You should see

A star * next to orbstack. If the star is somewhere else, type docker context use orbstack and press Return.

docs.title: 2. New versions arrive
docs.text:
tail -3 ~/Library/Logs/quota-update.log

You should see

The last line says done:. If it says unauthorized, do Quota's GitHub sign-in below.

docs.title: 3. The tunnels are up
docs.text:
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}  {{.Status}}' | grep tunnel

You should see

quota-staff-tunnel and quota-tunnel, both Up. If one is missing: docker start quota-staff-tunnel quota-tunnel.

docs.title: 4. The search helper runs
docs.text:
brew services list | grep ollama

You should see

ollama started. If it says anything else: brew services restart ollama.

docs.title: Quota's GitHub sign-in
docs.text:
The Mac downloads every new version from GitHub, signed in with a read-only key (a "token"). If the update log says unauthorized, the sign-in is gone or the token expired.

  1. Ask the developer for a new GitHub token with only read:packages (or make one on GitHub: your picture, top right → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token, tick only read:packages).

  2. On the office Mac, type this (change <github-user> to the GitHub username):

    DOCKER_CONFIG=~/quota/deploy/.docker docker login ghcr.io -u <github-user>

  3. When it asks for Password, paste the token and press Return. Nothing shows while you paste. That is normal.

  4. Within 2 minutes the Mac installs whatever was released. Check with step 2 above.

The token is a password

Never put it in chat, e-mail or on this site.

docs.title: The automatic jobs
docs.text:
Job When Its log in ~/Library/Logs/ Install a released version Every 2 minutes quota-update.log Copy backups off the Mac Every night at 03:15 quota-offsite.log Prove the backups can be restored Every Sunday quota-restore.log (appears after the first Sunday)

To see them: launchctl list | grep quota. To put them back after a reinstall: cd ~/quota/deploy && ./install-macos.sh.

docs.title: If you see something else
docs.text:
You see Do this "I pressed Release but nothing changed" Step 2. unauthorized: the sign-in above. FAILED ... rolled back: the new version was refused; tell the developer. Cannot connect to the Docker daemon Open OrbStack from Applications. Wait a minute. Then step 1. After a power cut nothing came back Someone must log in at the Mac once. Then check OrbStack is open. Mail search finds words but not meanings Step 4.

Last checked: 2026-11-11

docs.title: Passwords and keys
docs.text: When to use this: A password was shared by mistake, someone left, or a user is locked out. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: An administrator login for a locked-out user. For the keys: the Terminal on the office Mac (connect).

docs.title: A user is locked out
docs.text: Five wrong sign-in attempts in fifteen minutes lock the account for fifteen minutes. Wait fifteen minutes, or an administrator can reset the password in the app: Administration → Users.

docs.title: Sign everyone out and replace the signing key
docs.text:
The signing key (JWT_SECRET) proves a sign-in is genuine. Changing it signs everyone out.

  1. Make a new random key and copy what it prints (one long line of letters and numbers):
openssl rand -hex 32
  1. Open the settings file:
cd ~/quota
nano deploy/.env
  1. With the arrow keys, go to the line that starts with JWT_SECRET=. Delete what is after the = and paste the new key. Change nothing else.
  2. Save and close: press Ctrl O, then Return, then Ctrl X.
  3. Restart:
docker compose -p quota -f deploy/compose.yml -f deploy/compose.office.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d

Never change MAIL_SECRET_KEY

MAIL_SECRET_KEY in deploy/.env locks the staff mailboxes' passwords inside the database. If it changes, or is lost, every connected mailbox has to be connected again by its owner. Changing JWT_SECRET is safe as long as MAIL_SECRET_KEY stays as it is.

docs.title: Other keys on the Mac
docs.text: Key Where If it leaks Tunnel tokens A token file next to each tunnel's start script Make a new token in Cloudflare and restart that tunnel. See How staff and clients reach it. GitHub download token ~/quota/deploy/.docker Delete it on GitHub, make a new read-only one. See The office Mac. New-mail pop-up keys (VAPID_*) deploy/.env Make a new pair; staff then allow the pop-ups again once.

docs.title: Change the database password
docs.text: Do not do this alone: the password is stored in two places (the database and the settings file). Ask the developer.

docs.title: The settings file
docs.text: deploy/.env holds every secret. It is never in git. Keep a copy in the team password manager, because if the server is lost the file is lost too.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• After a key change, you are asked to sign in again.
  • A new password lets the user in.

Last checked: 2026-11-11
